title: An r-adaptive finite element method using neural networks for parametric self-adjoint elliptic problems

split.decision: Original archived paper test (120 rows) retained exactly, verified against archived mesh/energy arrays. Carve 20% of original 280 training rows: 56 validation rows chosen by numpy RandomState(20261030).permutation from non-corners; retain four forced training corners, leaving 224 training rows. Files sorted by original integer row id. Hidden split details are operator-only.

baseline.paper_ref: Table 5 N=10 Test: 0.1933; reproduced 0.1916202678384128. Benchmark carves validation from original training and retrains independently.

allowed_changes: coefficient-to-mesh predictor architecture, internal representation, training surrogate loss and optimizer
training-time FEM/mesh optimization on the training data, distillation and equivalent geometry-preserving prediction implementations
When retaining the supplied training pipeline, changing only --lr=0.01, --lr-schedule=fixed or --steps=1400000 does not count as a method improvement.
fixed_contract: Learn a reusable coefficient-to-mesh predictor for the fixed parametric multi-material L-shaped elliptic PDE, minimizing the original Q1 Ritz-energy relative error.
fixed L-shaped domain, material coefficient meanings, forcing, homogeneous Dirichlet conditions and supplied coefficient split
conforming Q1 evaluation with10 elements/11 ordered nodes per axis including0,0.5,1; original reference Ritz-energy error
offline learning followed by parameter-to-mesh prediction, with no prediction-time FEM/PDE solve or fresh instance-specific mesh optimization
Supplied data/splits, evaluation metric, trusted evaluator and lawful information access.
method_freedom_review.budget_policy: agent overall deadline; separate overall formal replay budget

turning held-out parametric prediction into fresh per-instance FEM/mesh optimization, reconstructing withheld coefficient rows or using reference-energy lookup tables
Training or fitting reusable model state or learned preprocessing on validation features or labels, including final train+val refits or validation-based distillation.
